ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Drought can promote the synthesis of abscisic acid (ABA) in plants. Seedlings of the wild type and an ABA-deficient mutant of a certain plant grown under normal water conditions were taken and subjected to moderate drought treatment. The growth amounts of stems and leaves and roots within a certain period of time were measured, and the results are shown in the figure. Answer the question: If an appropriate amount of ABA is applied to the mutant seedlings subjected to drought treatment, how is it inferred that the transpiration rate of plant leaves will change, so as to respond to changes in the environment?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the left curve of the figure, the drought treatment time is the horizontal axis, and the increase value of stem and leaf length is the vertical axis. As the treatment time is prolonged, the stem and leaf growth amount curve of the ABA-deficient mutant is higher than that of the wild type. In the right curve, the drought treatment time is the horizontal axis, and the increase value of root length is the vertical axis. As the treatment time is prolonged, the root growth amount curve of the wild type is higher than that of the mutant. Then reason: Drought will promote ABA synthesis in plants, and ABA is an important hormone for plants to cope with drought. The wild type can synthesize ABA, showing inhibition of aboveground growth and promotion of root growth to adapt to drought; the ABA-deficient mutant lacks this regulation. If an appropriate amount of ABA is applied to the mutant seedlings subjected to drought treatment, ABA can promote stomatal closure, thereby reducing water loss, so the leaf transpiration rate will decrease.
